Priya (ACME): hey team — our ingestion pipeline started failing with 401s a few minutes ago after we switched our SSO config. seen this error: { "error": { "type": "invalid_api_key", "message": "API key not recognized or expired" } }

Priya (ACME): snippet from our prod log (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9....
response: 401 {"error":{"type":"invalid_api_key"}}
```

Liam (Support): thanks for the trace. quick flag: that token begins with `eyJ` which looks like a JWT (OIDC/OAuth). Redwood API keys are opaque tokens (like `rwd_` or `svc_` prefixes). Using an OIDC access token will return invalid_api_key. Did you swap auth types during the SSO rollout?

Priya (ACME): yes we flipped to OIDC for console auth but I assumed the same browser token would work for API calls. my bad.

Liam (Support): totally understandable — common confusion. Two quick checks: (1) confirm the value in your secrets manager is the Redwood API key (not an OIDC access token). (2) ensure there are no accidental quotes/newlines when loading env vars. Example to validate locally:
```
# print raw bytes to detect trailing chars
printf "%s" "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | od -c | head
```
If you see `\"` or `\\n` at the end, trim them.

Priya (ACME): I pulled the key from our AWS Secrets Manager and it does start with `rwd_`. swapped into the service and one worker pod immediately started succeeding. but two older pods still 401.

Chen (Eng): checking audit logs — I see a key rotation event yesterday at 2028-02-03T03:12:45Z: key id `svc_b7c9` revoked, and a new key `svc_8d4a` created. looks like some hosts never picked up the new secret. audit snippet: `2028-02-03T03:12:45Z api_key.revoke actor=priya@acme.com key_id=svc_b7c9`

Asha (SRE): on the running pods that 401, can you run this to see what env var they actually have?
```
kubectl exec -it <pod> -- sh -c 'printf "%s" "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | sed -n l'
```
If the output shows a trailing single-quote or `\n` then the secret template might have added quotes. Also check if a legacy deploy manifest still references `svc_b7c9`.

Priya (ACME): good catch — one pod had the old key masked as `rwd_abc...` (last four chars b7c9) in the env. redeployed and all pods now return 200.

Liam (Support): great. summary for the ticket: cause = OIDC JWT used in place of Redwood API key + one service instance still using revoked key `svc_b7c9`. remediation = swap in valid `rwd_`/`svc_` API key, rotate any exposed keys, redeploy services, and verify secrets are loaded without extra quotes/newlines.

Chen (Eng): small follow-up — if anyone else is automating token exchange, note that exchanging an OIDC code for an access token (from your IdP) does not produce a Redwood API key. Only keys created in Console or via the API Key creation endpoint are valid for requests to api.redwood.ai.

Priya (ACME): thanks everyone. can you open a follow-up to scan for lingering `svc_b7c9` references across our infra?

Support Bot: ticket #SUP-2028-314 opened (assignee: Liam). escalation flagged to SRE for org scan.

Asha (SRE): will run a quick grep across manifests and secrets in config repo and report back. will also add a short note to our runbook about distinguishing console keys vs OIDC tokens.

Priya (ACME): appreciate the help — saved our ingestion job. :pray:
